title: spec review: P21/P27/P28/P30/P31 closing the loop: context evaluation suite over fixture tasks (seven categories, both modes), promotion evidence for the shadow features from the scorecards, and the unified `orchestrator scorecard --economy` view (v2)
spec:
Depends on the shadow features being merged: T-0800 (context router wiring), T-0802 (tool disclosure), T-0814 (conditional instructions), T-0831 (handoffs), T-0809 (read economy). Facts: promotion.evaluate needs {n, first_pass_delta, fix_rounds_delta, gate_success_delta, review_findings_delta, accepted_cost_delta, accepted_tokens_delta, latency_delta, security_ok}; context_scorecard, handoff_scorecard, read_economy and tool_catalog expose per-role/per-class rows; decision_log rows carry every shadow decision; the harness (tests/_harness.py) gives a temp ORCH_ROOT.
Do:
1. orchestrator/context_eval.py (new): fixture task builders for the seven P31 categories (localized_fix, cross_cutting, security, test_failure, documentation, review, repeated_fix_round), each a small synthetic worktree built under a temp dir (a few python files, a test file, a failing-output blob, an .md file) so no network or model is needed. `run(category, root)` builds the execute (or review) packet with every feature mode off and again with the modes in shadow, then reads the shadow meta (routed_tokens, routed_reduction_ratio, routed_hidden, instruction_tokens_modular, tool_tokens_minimal) and returns {"category", "candidate_tokens", "presented_tokens", "routed_tokens", "reduction", "hidden", "instruction_delta", "tool_delta", "expectation": {"min_reduction", "max_reduction"}, "within_expectation": bool, "must_keep": [...], "kept": bool}. Expectations from the brief: localized_fix large reduction (≥0.4), cross_cutting modest (0.1–0.4), security keeps security instructions and security-path evidence FULL (kept check), test_failure keeps failing output and the named tests FULL, documentation summaries over full chunks (no source_chunk FULL), review packet has diff + acceptance + interfaces and no implementation transcript, repeated_fix_round reuses prior evidence (evidence ids overlap with the first round ≥ 0.8). Every number is deterministic (chars//4).
2. `orchestrator context-eval` CLI: runs all categories, prints a table, exits 1 when any within_expectation or kept is False (so it can gate a future active flip); `--json`.
3. promotion.py evidence loaders for context_router, tool_disclosure, conditional_instructions, handoff_routing: n = number of runs carrying that feature's shadow keys (from runs jsonl context objects / decision rows), accepted_tokens_delta = -(avg reduction) as the efficiency signal ONLY when the context-eval suite passed in the same report (P21: shadow cannot show quality deltas because packets are unchanged; set first_pass_delta etc. to None and add reason "shadow_quality_unmeasured" so evaluate() returns stay, never promote, until an active A/B exists); context_recovery_rate placeholder from read_economy (evidence_available reads that happened after HIDE decisions for the same path, per task) reported as a number with n.
4. `orchestrator scorecard --economy`: one view joining context (P27), tool economy (P28), handoffs (P29) and read economy per role and task class, plus the promotion report for the four features and the last context-eval result; `--json`.
5. docs/context-economy/10-evaluation.md (≤80 lines): the seven fixtures and their expectations, how to read --economy, what promotion needs before any mode goes active (the P30 list: sample size, non-inferior quality, measurable efficiency, recovery rate low), the revert paths per feature.
Tests (unittest): tests/test_context_eval.py::test_localized_fix_reduces_and_keeps_scope_full, ::test_security_fixture_keeps_security_evidence_full, ::test_test_failure_fixture_keeps_failing_output_full, ::test_documentation_fixture_has_no_full_source_chunks, ::test_repeated_fix_round_reuses_evidence, ::test_cli_exit_code_reflects_expectations; tests/test_promotion.py::test_shadow_features_never_promote_without_quality_evidence.
Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally.

SPEC v2 (2026-09-22 20:40) after spec review T-0838 (request_changes), binding on top of v1:
- promotion.evaluate(): for the four shadow features (context_router, tool_disclosure, conditional_instructions, handoff_routing) any None among first_pass_delta / fix_rounds_delta / gate_success_delta / review_findings_delta caps the recommendation at "stay" with reason "shadow_quality_unmeasured", regardless of cost or token deltas. Test tests/test_promotion.py::test_shadow_features_never_promote_without_quality_evidence asserts exactly that path (all quality deltas None, accepted_tokens_delta negative, n above min_samples → stay).
- Packet building in both modes, exact mechanism: orchestrator/spawn.py is added to scope; spawn.packet(task, worktree, *, cfg=None) and the internal builders that read Pool().cfg accept an explicit cfg override (when given, no Pool() construction; existing callers unchanged). context_eval.run builds the packet twice with two cfg dicts derived from the harness pool.toml (modes off vs shadow) and never mutates the global pool.toml. Add tests/test_spawn.py::test_packet_accepts_cfg_override (same fixture task, cfg with context_router off vs shadow: identical packet text, shadow meta only in shadow).
- context_scorecard.build(): add a per-(role, task_class) grouping (task_class via attribution.task_class of the run's task, "unknown" when the task is gone) mirroring read_economy.summary and handoff_scorecard.by_start, so --economy joins on (role, task_class) across all four sources.
- Tool economy (P28) figures in --economy come from context_scorecard's existing tool_tokens_disclosed / tool_tokens_minimal / tool_reduction fields; tool_catalog.py is not a dependency and stays out of scope.
- tests/test_context_scorecard.py exists (six tests after T-0800/T-0814); extend it in place and keep every current test green.
acceptance: `uv run orchestrator context-eval` and `uv run orchestrator scorecard --economy` run; docs/context-economy/10-evaluation.md exists; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

risks.issue: context_eval.run(category, root) is specced to build fixtures 'under a temp dir', but spawn.py's shadow path (_shadow_route -> decision_log.record and evidence.EvidencePool, whose path is STATE/'evidence'/f'{goal}.jsonl') always writes to the global STATE = ROOT/'.orchestrator', not to the fixture's `root`. STATE is fixed at process-import time from ORCH_ROOT and nothing in the spec redirects it per-call. Under the test harness this is masked because ORCH_ROOT already points at a temp dir, but running the real `uv run orchestrator context-eval` CLI on a live orchestrator checkout will write synthetic decision_log rows and evidence-pool files for fake fixture task ids into the production .orchestrator state on every invocation, corrupting the exact telemetry (context_router/tool_disclosure/conditional_instructions decision rows, runs jsonl context objects) that promotion.py and context_scorecard.py read for real shadow evidence. No item addresses isolating or cleaning up these writes for a live run.

Item 3 requires accepted_tokens_delta to be set for context_router/tool_disclosure/conditional_instructions/handoff_routing 'ONLY when the context-eval suite passed in the same report', and item 4 requires `scorecard --economy` to show 'the last context-eval result'. Neither collect(feature, root) nor report(cfg, root) has a parameter or documented artifact carrying a context-eval pass/fail signal between commands, and the CLI in item 2 only 'prints a table' / supports --json, with no specified persistence file (contrast orchestrator/bench.py, which persists STATE/'bench.json' for exactly this kind of cross-command reuse). No acceptance test exercises 'suite passed' gating accepted_tokens_delta, or 'last context-eval result' appearing in --economy, so this requirement cannot be verified and an executor has no defined insertion point to satisfy it correctly.

Spec v2 says packet() and 'the internal builders that read Pool().cfg' accept an explicit cfg override, but only tests/test_spawn.py::test_packet_accepts_cfg_override is listed, which exercises packet() alone. review_packet() independently constructs Pool().cfg three times (security_paths at 627, review_diff_chars at 665, and the shadow-route cfg at 670), and the context_eval 'review' category fixture (diff + acceptance + interfaces, no implementation transcript) requires building a review packet in both off/shadow modes without touching the real pool.toml — impossible unless review_packet also takes a cfg override. Without a named test for it, an executor can pass the single acceptance test while leaving review_packet dependent on global Pool() state, breaking determinism for the 'review' fixture category.

suggested_spec_changes: Specify how decision_log/evidence writes triggered by shadow packet-building during context_eval are isolated from production STATE for a live `orchestrator context-eval` run (e.g. context_eval.run must set/override STATE or ORCH_ROOT for the duration of the call, or the CLI must require/enforce a --root pointing at a scratch orchestrator root) — and add an acceptance test asserting no writes land under the live .orchestrator directory.

Name the persistence artifact for context-eval results (e.g. STATE/'context_eval.json', written by the CLI after each run) and thread a 'suite_passed' value from that artifact into promotion.collect()/evaluate() for the four shadow features and into context_scorecard/--economy's 'last context-eval result'; add a test asserting accepted_tokens_delta is None when no context-eval report exists or it failed.

Extend test_spawn.py::test_packet_accepts_cfg_override (or add a sibling test) to also cover review_packet(task, cfg=...) so the 'review' category fixture's cfg override is actually verified, not just packet()'s.
